printed_page_note: no printed page number is on this exposure. A continuation sheet carries its number in the top margin above the SCHOOLS block, and that margin is in shadow here; the leaf is identified by its FamilySearch image id alone.
division: S. W. Sherman (as written in the printed heading)
line_count_note: 31, and this CONFIRMS the count coverage.json already carried rather than correcting it - but it is now measured instead of eyeballed. The row grid is fitted to the TOTAL column's own ink: 30 ink bands at the 45-grey-level threshold, of which the band at y2597-2724 is two entries and not one (127 px against a line pitch of about 80, and three components where its neighbours have one). Dropping the threshold to 30 and to 22 grey levels finds no further line, so no entry is being lost under it. A blank line's worth of space stands between line 12 and line 13 - 135 px where the pitch is 80 - and it carries no ink in any column.
form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: twelve SLAVES columns (six male, six female age bands); TOTAL - number of persons in each family; seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns (mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures and trades, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, learned professions and engineers); PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (ages, names); six DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND, AND INSANE WHITE PERSONS columns; four of the same for coloured persons; and seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns. A blank cell on this form is a zero and is recorded as 0.
right_edge_note: Unlike 33S7-9YYJ-V4, this exposure carries the whole form: the seventh SCHOOLS column - white persons over 20 years of age who cannot read and write - stands complete inside the frame at about x3760, and it is blank. Nothing on this leaf is recorded unread for want of the exposure. The column of numerals visible beyond x3900 belongs to the next leaf and is not read here.
grid_note: The column grid is measured off the leaf and not assumed, because these rules LEAN. A column-darkness profile taken in a 300 px band at the head of the body (centre y742) puts the nine printed rules of the TOTAL-and-industry run at 1287, 1476, 1546, 1609, 1675, 1757, 1837, 1917 and 1981 px, and the same profile at the foot (centre y3034) puts them at 1276, 1468, 1537, 1601, 1667, 1747, 1828, 1909 and 1973 - eight to eleven pixels of lean over the leaf, against column widths of 63 to 82. The grid is interpolated linearly between those two measurements. It is then CHECKED against the printed heading before any cell is cut: the interpolated column named `mining` is the one under the printed word Mining, `commerce` the one under Commerce, and `navigation_canals_lakes_rivers` the one under Navigation of canals, lakes, and rivers. All seven agree, which is what fixes the three written industry columns as COMMERCE, MANUFACTURES AND TRADES and LEARNED PROFESSIONS rather than their neighbours; the footer row agrees with the same assignment. tools/read_census_continuation.py refuses this leaf outright - 'no industry run bracketed by TOTAL and PENSIONERS' - because it fits one profile over the whole body; that is T-0761's fix and this reading did not wait for it.
exposure_note: A grey, low-contrast leaf. Ink is taken as 45 grey levels below a 25-pixel Gaussian of the crop itself rather than against a flat threshold, because the exposure falls off toward the gutter. Two rules cross the body horizontally: the head rule at y587 and the foot rule at y3186, with the enumerator's footer row between y3186 and y3251.
alphabet_note: The digits are read against a LABELLED alphabet in the same enumerator's hand rather than by eye alone. 33S7-9YYN-3CF6 is S. W. Sherman's too, its 27 line totals are committed, and its figures can therefore be cropped with their values known: line 11 gives this hand's 1 (a single slanted stroke thickening to a bulb at the foot), lines 5 and 15 its 2 (a top loop, a descending diagonal, and a base stroke running left to right at the foot), line 10 its 3 (a small upper bowl over a larger lower bowl, both opening left, and NO base stroke), lines 12 to 14 its 4 (two strokes), line 3 its 5, line 16 its 6, line 2 its 8 and line 9 its 10. The distinction that carries most of this leaf is the one between the 2 and the 3, and it is the base stroke: the 2 has one and the 3 does not. Two of this leaf's own columns then check the alphabet without being told the answer - commerce reads 24 against a printed 24, and manufactures and trades reads 5 against a printed 5.
closure_note: The enumerator footed four columns and left the rest of the footer row blank. Those printed totals are transcribed under `footer_as_read` and every column is checked against them in `column_closure`. A column that does not close keeps its residual and its reading is NOT adjusted to make the total come out - the residual is the finding, and the reading goes to `cells_first_pass` where nothing downstream can consume it.

footer_as_read.total_footing_note: Three glyphs: 1-1-7. The middle glyph is a thin short slant with a tick at its foot. It is NOT this hand's 0, and that is now evidenced rather than asserted - 33S7-9YYN-3CF6 line 9 is a committed 10 in the same hand, and its 0 is a closed filled oval nothing like this mark. 117 is therefore the reading and 107 is kept as the alternate T-0656 named, because the glyph is short enough to be argued. The line-by-line reading below reaches neither figure and so settles nothing between them.
footer_as_read.learned_professions_footing_note: One glyph, in the palest part of the footer row: a small hook over a long stroke descending to the left. Read 2. A 9 is named as the alternate because the hook could be a bowl; the two lines of the column read 1 and 1, which agrees with the 2, and that agreement is recorded as agreement rather than used to strike the alternate out.
footer_as_read.footer_blank_columns_note: The footer row of this leaf carries FOUR figures and no others - 117 under TOTAL, 24 under commerce, 5 under manufactures and trades and 2 under the learned professions. Mining, agriculture, navigation of the ocean and navigation of canals, lakes and rivers are unfooted, and so are the twelve slaves columns, the pensioners columns, the ten deaf/dumb/blind/insane columns and the seven schools columns.

total.why: The 31 lines read at magnification come to 84 against a footing of 117 (alternate 107). The column does NOT close and is NOT committed; every line's figure is kept as `cells_first_pass`. A residual of -33 over 31 lines is far too large to be a slip in one or two glyphs, so this is a disagreement about the leaf and not about a digit: either the reading is wrong in a way this pass cannot see, or the footing is not the sum of the column above it. What the reading DOES establish is that the entries are single digits - there is no ink at all in the left half of the TOTAL cell on any line of the body, 445 pixels of speckle over 2,580 rows - so no hidden tens digit accounts for the difference. Two independent checks say the reading method is sound where it can be checked: commerce closes exactly at 24 and manufactures and trades at 5, both read blind and both against the enumerator's own figure.

mining.why: blank on all 31 lines and unfooted; there is nothing to check. The zeros are committed under the form's rule that a blank cell is a zero.

agriculture.why: blank on all 31 lines and unfooted. Two marks stand inside the column and neither is a numeral: a broken horizontal smear at y1784-1803 and a small blot at y2274-2284, both sitting BETWEEN line centres rather than on one. They are named here and refused rather than read.

commerce.why: 14 figures read at magnification sum to exactly the enumerator's own footing. Committed.

manufactures_and_trades.why: 3 figures - 1, 1 and 3 - sum to the printed 5. Committed.

navigation_ocean.why: blank on all 31 lines and unfooted.

navigation_canals_lakes_rivers.why: blank on all 31 lines and unfooted.

learned_professions_and_engineers.why: 2 figures, both 1, against a footing read as 2 with 9 named as its alternate. Committed on the primary reading of the footing.

what_the_sheet_says: Thirty-one households on a leaf that is worked, not farmed. Fourteen lines return somebody in COMMERCE and three in MANUFACTURES AND TRADES, two in the LEARNED PROFESSIONS, and not one person in agriculture, in mining or in either navigation column - the exact opposite of 33S7-9YYJ-V4, whose 21 households return 33 in agriculture and nobody in anything else. Twenty-four people in commerce out of a footed page population of 117 is a town's profile and not a township's. No slave is returned on any line, no pensioner, nobody deaf, dumb, blind or insane, and no school. It is LATER EVIDENCE under this domain's rule and it names nobody - the names are on a left sheet nobody has found.

pairing.test: both keys - the count of lines that enumerate a household, and the page population read off the TOTAL footing - against every left sheet read anywhere in the deposit.
pairing.result: Refused on both keys by T-0656: neither 117 nor 107 is any left sheet's page population anywhere in the deposit, and the five 31-line left sheets of this group foot 175, 151, 160, 195 and 181.
pairing.what_this_reading_changes: The LINE-COUNT key is unchanged at 31 and is now a measured reading rather than a count to the nearest line. The PAGE-POPULATION key is where this reading bites, and it weakens it: the 31 lines of the TOTAL column read 84, so the footing the key rests on is not corroborated by the column it foots. That does not make 117 wrong - the footing is what the enumerator wrote, and it is what a left sheet would have to match - but a key whose own column refuses it should be tested as a weak key, and a pairing that turns on it alone should not be taken. The line-count key is the sounder of the two on this leaf.
pairing.not_ruled_here: 33S7-9YYJ-W6, printed page 232, is a 31-line left sheet of this same division and is the leaf T-0736 is looking for a continuation for. It is recorded here as an observation and NOT as a pairing: W6's own footings give it 193 free persons against this leaf's 117, which the page-population key refuses. T-0736 owned that question and dev has since answered it: T-0911 found printed 232 continuation on NARA microfilm M704 roll 57, leaf n167, and paired it there. This leaf is not it, and the refusal above stands on its own evidence.
